questions.question: Preconception nutrition refers to the nutritional status of a woman / a). During labour b). After childbirth c). Before conception d). During lactation
questions.solution_html:
• Option C
  • Maintains normal menstrual cycle. Causes menstrual irregularities.
  • Prolactin-Stimulates the development of mammary glands and milk synthesis. Its level
  • increases during pregnancy. Actual milk secretion is inhibited during pregnancy due to high
  • estrogen and progesterone levels. ((1.5 Mark))

  • A Non-lactating woman- 1,660–2,720 kcal/day, lactating woman- an additional 600
  • kcal during 0-6 months and additional 520 kcal during 7-12 months.Extra energy

questions.question: Explain how Breast milk is expressed with a Breast Pump
questions.solution_html:
• Steps
  • ● Wash hands: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water and ensure the breast pump
  • and its parts are clean.
  • ● Prepare the breast: Sit comfortably and gently massage the breasts to stimulate milk
  • flow.
  • ● Position the pump: Place the breast shield over the nipple, ensuring the nipple is
  • centred.
  • ● Express the milk: Switch on the electric pump or operate the manual pump. Start with
  • gentle suction and gradually increase to a comfortable level until milk flows.
  • ● Collect and store: Express milk from both breasts, pour it into a clean, sterile container
  • label it with the date and time, and store it safely according to breast milk storage
  • guidelines. ((5 mark))

questions.question: Explain how gastrointestinal changes help meet the nutritional demands of / pregnancy.
questions.solution_html:
• pregnancy
  • ● Decreased gastrointestinal motility: Progesterone slows intestinal movement, allowing
  • more time for nutrient and water absorption.
  • ● Nausea and vomiting: Hormonal changes, mainly increased hCG and estrogen, may
  • affect food intake, especially during the first trimester.
  • ● Heartburn: Relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter causes acid reflux.
  • ● Constipation: Reduced intestinal motility and increased water absorption cause
  • constipation.
  • ● Increased appetite: Higher energy and nutrient requirements support fetal growth and
  • maternal health.
  • ● Displacement of stomach and intestines: The enlarging uterus compresses the digestive
  • organs, causing early fullness and reduced meal capacity. ((1 mark) for each point)
questions.final_answer: organs, causing early fullness and reduced meal capacity. ( for each point)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the factors influencing fetal growth and development.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Genetic factors: Determine foetal size, growth and organ development.
  • ● Maternal nutrition: Nutrient deficiencies may cause low birth weight and IUGR.
  • ● Placental function: Supplies oxygen and nutrients to the foetus.
  • ● Hormonal regulation: Hormones control foetal growth and organ maturation.
  • ● Intrauterine environment: Maternal health, infections, smoking and alcohol influence
  • foetal development. ((1 mark) for each point)
